title: IMF — International Monetary Fund
shortDescription: Bretton Woods' monetary watchdog: surveillance, lending, SDRs, and exactly how it differs from the World Bank.
genZNote: The IMF checks your economy's vitals; the World Bank funds your economy's gym membership.

sections.heading: Full Form, Bretton Woods Background, Headquarters
bullets: Origin: created at the Bretton Woods Conference (Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA, July 1944), alongside the World Bank (then the IBRD) — both are sometimes called the 'Bretton Woods Twins'.
A UN specialized agency, but functionally and financially independent — funded by member quotas, not the UN budget.

sections.heading: Objectives and Functions
bullets: Promote international monetary cooperation and exchange rate stability.
Surveillance — monitoring member economies and the global economy, issuing regular assessments (e.g. the World Economic Outlook).
Lending — providing financial support to countries facing balance-of-payments problems, usually attached to policy-reform conditions.
Technical assistance and capacity development for member countries' fiscal, monetary and financial institutions.

sections.heading: Special Drawing Rights (SDR) and Quota System
sections.body:
The Special Drawing Right (SDR) is an international reserve asset created by the IMF (1969) to supplement member countries' official reserves — its value is set daily from a basket of major currencies (US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen, British pound). It is NOT a currency itself and cannot be used directly for private transactions — only between IMF members and certain official holders.

Each member is assigned a 'quota', broadly based on its relative size in the world economy. Quotas determine a member's maximum financial commitment to the IMF, its voting power, and its access to IMF financing — larger economies have larger quotas and correspondingly larger voting shares.

sections.heading: Governance
bullets: Board of Governors — the highest decision-making body, one governor per member (usually the finance minister or central bank governor).
Executive Board — conducts day-to-day business; 24 executive directors represent member countries or constituencies.
Managing Director — by convention, always a European; the Managing Director chairs the Executive Board and is IMF's chief of staff.

sections.heading: IMF and India
bullets: India is a founding member of the IMF (1945).
India famously borrowed from the IMF in 1991 amid a severe balance-of-payments crisis, accepting conditional economic reforms that catalysed India's 1991 liberalization.
India has since become a net creditor/contributor rather than a borrower, and has periodically supported increased quota/voting shares for emerging economies.

sections.heading: Current Leadership (verified)
sections.body: Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria) has been IMF Managing Director since October 2019 — by the informal convention that has held since Bretton Woods, the IMF's head is European while the World Bank's head is American.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The IMF is the Bretton Woods institution (1944, operational 1947, HQ Washington D.C.) that promotes monetary cooperation and exchange-rate stability through surveillance and balance-of-payments lending.
keyFacts: Created at Bretton Woods, July 1944; began operations 1947. HQ: Washington, D.C.
SDR = IMF's international reserve asset (since 1969) — not a currency for private use.
Quota size determines a member's voting power and financing access.
India borrowed from IMF in 1991, triggering the 1991 economic liberalization reforms.
Current MD: Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgaria), since October 2019 — MD is by convention always European.
commonConfusion: SDR is a reserve asset/unit of account, NOT a currency you can spend directly — don't call it 'IMF's currency'.

highYieldFacts: IMF and World Bank both trace to the Bretton Woods Conference, July 1944 — the 'Bretton Woods Twins'.
By convention: IMF Managing Director is European; World Bank President is American.
India's 1991 IMF loan directly preceded India's economic liberalization reforms.
commonTraps: Don't confuse IMF's role (short-term monetary/balance-of-payments stability) with the World Bank's role (long-term development financing).
SDR value is a basket of currencies (USD, EUR, RMB, JPY, GBP) — it is not pegged to gold or any single currency.
mustRemember: IMF quota = financial commitment + voting power + access to financing, all in one number.
IMF began financial operations in 1947, though it was created in 1944.

confusedTerms.distinction: IMF focuses on short-term monetary/exchange-rate stability and balance-of-payments support; World Bank focuses on long-term development financing and poverty reduction. Both were born at Bretton Woods (1944).

possibleQuestions: At which conference were the IMF and World Bank created, and in which year?
What does SDR stand for, and what is it NOT (a common trap)?
